lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: modeling physical objects with geometric shapes
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: modeling physical objects with geometric shapes

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: Mass 48 g, volume 6 cm³. Density and float?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A square patio of side 9 m is to be paved at $3 per square metre. Find the total cost, and state which quantity the cost is proportional to.
choices: $108; the cost is proportional to the perimeter
$243; the cost is proportional to the area
$243; the cost is proportional to the side length
$27; the cost is proportional to the area

items.prompt: Find the volume of a square pyramid with base edge 3 and height 7. Leave π in the answer where it appears.
Describe the cross-section formed by a square pyramid cut by a plane parallel to its base.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A solid object has mass 180 g and volume 18 cm³. Find its density, and state whether it would float in water (density 1 g/cm³).
A square patio of side 12 m is to be paved at $17 per square metre. Find the total cost, and state which quantity the cost is proportional to.
choices: $204; the cost is proportional to the area
$2448; the cost is proportional to the side length
$2448; the cost is proportional to the area
$816; the cost is proportional to the perimeter

items.prompt: Find the volume of a square pyramid with base edge 4 and height 12. Leave π in the answer where it appears.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Describe the cross-section formed by a sphere cut by any plane that meets it in more than one point.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A solid object has mass 132 g and volume 11 cm³. Find its density, and state whether it would float in water (density 1 g/cm³).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
